item.title: Seattle Times and Newsday are the latest publications to sue OpenAI and Microsoft
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: Two more news organizations are suing OpenAI and Microsoft over the supposed use of their journalism to train AI.

item.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: The sheriff’s office said the hikers “were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required."

item.title: OpenAI confirms ‘wiki incident,’ says it’s ‘working on a framework’ for more disclosure
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: OpenAI acknowledged its role in a recently reported incident where AI agents took over a German wiki forum.

item.title: XDOF, just three months out of stealth, is in talks for a Series B at a $1.2B valuation
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: The round is being raised just months after the robot data startup exited from stealth.

item.title: OpenAI’s rogue agents keep escaping, with no formal process to investigate them
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: OpenAI’s latest agent swarm incident adds urgency to calls for independent investigations as researchers and lawmakers question whether AI labs should control the scope of their own safety reviews.

item.title: AI compute provider Nscale is looking for $3.5B in pre-IPO financing
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Nscale, which recently struck a $45 billion deal with Anthropic, is in talks to raise additional funds in anticipation of an upcoming IPO.

item.title: What will Apple’s John Ternus era look like?
item.dc:creator: Theresa Loconsolo
item.description: It’s officially the Ternus era at Apple.   Tim Cook stepped down as CEO this week, handing the company to former hardware chief John Ternus, whose first memo promised a “huge launch next week” — timing that puts Apple’s next iPhone event on his desk before he’s even settled in. Cook isn’t going far, though: he’s staying on as Executive Chairman, focused on the kind of policy […]

item.title: Another swarm of OpenAI agents reached the open internet without the frontier lab’s knowledge
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: It's the latest failure of OpenAI's internal monitoring and security systems.

item.title: Google’s Gemini Spark can now manage your Google Photos library
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Gemini Spark can edit and curate photo albums, create shared collections, turn photos into calendar events, and handle other Google Photos tasks for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

item.title: Less than 24 hours to apply for your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Side Event
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: Less than 24 hours left to apply to host a Side Event during TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 and make your mark in the Silicon Valley scene. Apply before the application closes tonight at midnight PT.

item.title: The sameness problem behind those unappetizing AI-generated menus
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: While restaurant owners might look to generative AI as a shortcut to sprucing up their menu, customers can viscerally sense that something is wrong with the food.

item.title: Crusoe reportedly raises $3B at a $30B valuation
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: The round came together after the data center developer reportedly secured a $13 billion contract with Jane Street.

item.title: Accel reportedly in talks to lead $1B round for Thinking Machines at $40B valuation
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: The high-profile startup's annual revenue run rate stands at over $100 million.

item.title: Abliteration.ai is making a business out of removing AI guardrails
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: Abliteration.AI is making powerful AI models without guardrails easier to access, arguing that giving defenders the same tools as bad actors could ultimately improve cybersecurity.

item.title: Meta is paying to peek at how you use their latest AI model
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: For its new Muse Spark model, intended for operating coding and other agents, Meta is offering an explicit discount averaging out to about 95% for users who "contribute" to the development of future models by sharing their prompts and model outputs.

item.title: OpenAI launches Astra, its powerful (and controversial) new model
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: OpenAI claims that Astra represents "a new frontier on computer and browser use," and that it handles tasks with unmatched "speed, accuracy, and safety."

item.title: Ollie is betting its focus on privacy can help it win the AI assistant race
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: The family-focused AI assistant wants access to the details of your everyday life, but says it won’t use that data to train AI models or share it with others.

item.title: Google’s latest AI weather model gives you no excuse to forget your umbrella
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: WeatherNext 3 is the latest wave of a sea change in meteorology brought out by deep learning techniques. Google says it will start feeding into weather information users see in search, Google Maps, and Gemini.
